content:
maria: FYI - saw a burst of OOMs hitting the paged-attn path on the dedicated gamma pool after the kernel-routing tweak rolled at 09:12. Failing on our long-seq smoke (4k tokens) intermittently.

ken: Can you paste the top logs + profiler snapshot for one of the failing runs?

maria: Pasting the relevant tail from the job + nvprof summary:
```
[2026-03-18T09:15:43Z] ERROR oom: allocation failed: requested=728MB, available=200MB, stack=serve::alloc
[2026-03-18T09:15:43Z] kernel-router: chose fast-attn-kv (heuristic seq>1024, batch_est=2.1)
[2026-03-18T09:15:43Z] blkmgr: blocks_in_use=18432 total_blocks=21500 frag_pct=26.9
[2026-03-18T09:15:43Z] eviction: last_compaction=120s ago, compaction_locked=false

nvprof summary: peak_alloc=8.9GB, total_allocated=29.3GB, memcpy_time=1.2s
previous baseline (before routing change): peak_alloc=6.2GB for same workload
```
kv cache stats: total_blocks=1_020_432, free_runs=74, avg_block_fill=0.62

leo: Hypothesis: the new routing picks fast-attn-kv which uses a larger per-layer workspace (different kernel implementation keeps extra temp buffers). For long seqs that multiplies workspace and pushes eviction past safe threshold.

sasha: Agreed. Quick mitigation ideas: cap per-request workspace and add a conservative fallback for long sequences. Example quick config we can flip on the pool: 
```yaml
# eng-config/dedicated/gamma.yaml (patch)
kernel_routing:
  prefer_fast_for_seq: 2048  # raise threshold to avoid premature fast-kernel picks
workspace:
  per_request_cap_mb: 2400  # cap workspace to avoid OOM spiral
blockmgr:
  reuse_threshold: 0.75  # prefer reuse over compaction if block is >=75% full
  compaction_freq_s: 60
```

maria: If I force KERNEL_FORCE_SAFE=1 on the pool (force safe kernels) the 4k job finished twice in a row locally. So kernel selection + workspace multiplier is the culprit.

deploy-bot: @ken started roll of config patch to gamma at 09:42 (dry run) :gear:

nora: We should also look at block manager policies: compaction is expensive (cpu+gpu sync) and with small blocks we pay a lot of compaction overhead. For this workload, larger blocks and more aggressive reuse reduce compaction churn. Maybe raise max_block_size from 64KB -> 128KB for long-seq traffic.

ryan: Quick numbers from profiler comparing baseline vs current patch: 
- baseline (old routing): avg_peak=6.2GB, p90_latency=420ms, compaction_cpu=0.9s/run
- after routing change: avg_peak=8.9GB, p90_latency=460ms, compaction_cpu=1.9s/run
Memory pressure increases linearly with sequence length beyond 2k due to workspace per-layer factor ~1.8x on fast-kernel. Flamegraph shows spikes at allocate_workspace() and blockmgr::compact().

ken: Action items (short):
1) revert kernel-routing threshold for gamma to previous value (ken)
2) push workspace per-request cap config (sasha)
3) bump blockmgr.max_block_size for dedicated pools with long-seq traffic and increase reuse_threshold (nora + eng-runtime)
4) longer-term: implement workspace pooling and extend kernel cost model to include workspace delta not just latency (ryan + eng-ml)

ken: I will pick up 1 & 3 for the emergency patch and coordinate with ops to monitor.\n
maria: created INF ticket with traces and perf artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345 — added heap profiles, nvprof dumps, and blockmgr traces.

sasha: I'll open a PR for the config patch and a small runtime guard (cap) with a unit test.

maria: thanks all :pray: let's keep this thread for updates, moving to incident channel if it escalates.
